html:
The Union of Krewo was an agreement sealed on 14 August 1385 at Kreva castle, in today's western Belarus, under which Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania would marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland and become King of Poland.

Jogaila promised to be baptised and to convert his pagan people, which led to the baptism of Lithuania in 1387. Crowned as Władysław II Jagiełło, he founded the Jagiellonian dynasty that ruled much of Central Europe. The joint power of Poland and Lithuania crushed the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald in 1410. The personal union grew into the Union of Lublin of 1569. Belarusian lands, then in Lithuania, came under strong Polish influence.
